questions.q:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
The top (M$) of a tower is observed from three points $P$, $Q$ and $R$ lying in a horizontal straight line which passes directly along the foot (N$) of the tower. The angles of elevations of $M$ from $P$, $Q$ and $R$ are $30°$, $45°$ and $60°$ respectively. Let $PQ = a$ and $QR = b$.

What is $PN$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Let $h$ be the height of the tower $MN$.

In $\triangle MNP$, $\tan 30^{}^{\circ} = \dfrac{h}{PN} \Rightarrow PN = h\sqrt{3}$

In $\triangle MNQ$, $\tan 45^{}^{\circ} = \dfrac{h}{QN} \Rightarrow QN = h$

In $\triangle MNR$, $\tan 60^{}^{\circ} = \dfrac{h}{RN} \Rightarrow RN = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{3}}$

Since the angles of elevation increase as we move closer to the tower, the points $P, Q, R$ lie on the same side of $N$ in the order $P, Q, R, N$.

Given $PQ = a$, we have $PN - QN = a$.

$h\sqrt{3} - h = a \Rightarrow h(\sqrt{3} - 1) = a$

$h = \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{3} - 1}$

Rationalizing the denominator, we get:

$h = \dfrac{a(\sqrt{3} + 1)}{(\sqrt{3} - 1)(\sqrt{3} + 1)} = \dfrac{a(\sqrt{3} + 1)}{2}$

We need to find $PN$, which is $h\sqrt{3}$:

$PN = \dfrac{a(\sqrt{3} + 1)}{2} \times \sqrt{3} = \left(\dfrac{3 + \sqrt{3}}{2}\right)a$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph: There are two points $P$ and $Q$ due south of a leaning tower, which leans towards north. $P$ is at a distance $x$ and $Q$ is at a distance $y$ from the foot of the tower $(x > y)$. The angles of elevation of the top of the tower from $P$ and $Q$ are $15^{{}^{\circ}}$ and $75^{{}^{\circ}}$ respectively.
Question: What is the length of the tower?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text{ Length$ of $the tower, } A B=\sqrt{h^2+z^2} \\ & =\sqrt{\frac{(x-y)^2}{12}+\left(\frac{2 \sqrt{3}(x-y)-3(x+y)}{6}\right)^2} \\ & =\frac{(x-y)}{2 \sqrt{3}} \sqrt{1+\left(2-\frac{\sqrt{3}(x+y)}{x-y}\right)^2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A man at $M$, standing 100 m away from the base (P$) of a chimney of height 50 m, observes the angle of elevation of the highest point (Q$) of the smoke to be $45°$. The highest point of the chimney is at $R$. Further $P$, $R$ and $Q$ are in a straight line and the straight line is perpendicular to $PM$. What is the angle $RMQ$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Let $PM$ be the distance of the man from the base of the chimney, so $PM = 100$ m.

Let $PR$ be the height of the chimney, so $PR = 50$ m.

Let $Q$ be the highest point of the smoke. The angle of elevation of $Q$ from $M$ is $\angle PMQ = 45^{}^{\circ}$.

In $\triangle PMQ$, $\tan(\angle PMQ) = \dfrac{PQ}{PM}$

$\tan(45^{}^{\circ}) = \dfrac{PQ}{100} \Rightarrow PQ = 100$ m.

In $\triangle PMR$, $\tan(\angle PMR) = \dfrac{PR}{PM} = \dfrac{50}{100} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

The required angle is $\angle RMQ = \angle PMQ - \angle PMR = 45^{}^{\circ} - \angle PMR$.

Taking tangent on both sides:

$\tan(\angle RMQ) = \tan(45^{}^{\circ} - \angle PMR) = \dfrac{\tan(45^{}^{\circ}) - \tan(\angle PMR)}{1 + \tan(45^{}^{\circ})\tan(\angle PMR)}$

$\tan(\angle RMQ) = \dfrac{1 - \dfrac{1}{2}}{1 + 1 \times \dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}}{\dfrac{3}{2}} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$\angle RMQ = \tan^{-1} \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)

Answer: $\tan^{-1} $\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph: There are two points $P$ and $Q$ due south of a leaning tower, which leans towards north. $P$ is at a distance $x$ and $Q$ is at a distance $y$ from the foot of the tower $(x > y)$. The angles of elevation of the top of the tower from $P$ and $Q$ are $15^{{}^{\circ}}$ and $75^{{}^{\circ}}$ respectively.
Question: If $\theta$ is the inclination of the tower to the horizontal, then what is $\cot \theta$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \therefore \quad z=\frac{h}{\tan 75^{{}^{\circ}}}-y=\frac{x-y}{2 \sqrt{3}} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{\sqrt{3}+1}-y \\ & =\frac{(x-y)}{2}\left[\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{3+\sqrt{3}} \times \frac{3-\sqrt{3}}{3-\sqrt{3}}\right]-y \\ & =\frac{x-y}{2}\left[\frac{3 \sqrt{3}-3-3+\sqrt{3}}{9-3}\right]-y \\ & =(x-y) \frac{[2 \sqrt{3}-3]}{6}-y=\frac{2 \sqrt{3}(x-y)-3(x+y)}{6} \\ & \cot \theta=\frac{z}{h}=\frac{2 \sqrt{3}(x-y)-3(x+y)}{6} \times \frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{x-y} \\ & =2-\frac{\sqrt{3}(x+y)}{x-y}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A vertical tower stands on a horizontal plane and is surmounted by a vertical flagstaff of height $h$. At a point on the plane the angles of elevation of the bottom and top of the flagstaff are $\theta$ and $2 \theta$ respectively. What is the height of the tower?
questions.solution: In $\triangle \mathrm{PBC}\tan \theta=\frac{B C}{P C}\Rightarrow \quad P C=B C \cot \theta...(i)$ In $\triangle P A C\begin{aligned} & \tan 2 \theta=\frac{h+B C}{P C} \\ \Rightarrow \quad & P C \tan 2 \theta=h+B C\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad B C \cdot \cot \theta \cdot \frac{2 \tan \theta}{1-\tan ^2 \theta}=h+B C \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{2 B C}{1-\tan ^2 \theta}-B C=h \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{1+\tan ^2 \theta}{1-\tan ^2 \theta} B C=h \\ & \Rightarrow \quad B C=\frac{1-\tan ^2 \theta}{1+\tan ^2 \theta} h=\cos 2 \theta \cdot h\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph: There are two points $P$ and $Q$ due south of a leaning tower, which leans towards north. $P$ is at a distance $x$ and $Q$ is at a distance $y$ from the foot of the tower $(x > y)$. The angles of elevation of the top of the tower from $P$ and $Q$ are $15^{{}^{\circ}}$ and $75^{{}^{\circ}}$ respectively.
Question: At what height is the top of the tower above the ground level?
questions.solution: In $\triangle A C Q \tan 75^{{}^{\circ}}=\frac{h}{z+y}\Rightarrow z=\frac{h}{\tan 75^{{}^{\circ}}}-y$ ...(i) In $\triangle A C P \tan 15^{{}^{\circ}}=\frac{h}{z+x}\Rightarrow z=\frac{h}{\tan 15^{{}^{\circ}}}-x$ ...(ii) From (i) and (ii) $\begin{aligned} & \frac{h}{\tan 15^{{}^{\circ}}}-\frac{h}{\tan 75^{{}^{\circ}}}=x-y \\ & \Rightarrow h\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{3-1}}-\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{\sqrt{3}+1}\right)=x-y \\ & {\left[\because\left[$\begin{array}{l} \because $\tan 75^{{}^{\circ}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{\sqrt{3}+1}$ \\ $\tan 75^{{}^{\circ}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{3}-1}$ \end{array}$\right]\right.} \\ & \Rightarrow h\left(\frac{3+1+2 \sqrt{3}-3-1+2 \sqrt{3}}{3-1}\right)=x-y \\ & \Rightarrow h(2 \sqrt{3})=x-y \Rightarrow h=\frac{x-y}{2 \sqrt{3}} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A ladder 6 m long reaches a point 6 m below the top of a vertical flagstaff. From the foot of the ladder, the elevation of the top of the flagstaff is $75^{{}^{\circ}}$. What is the height of the flagstaff?
questions.solution:
Let $A C$ is a flagstaff of length $h \mathrm{ m} and B D$ is a ladder of length 6 m . Point $B$ is below the top of the flagstaff, such that $A B=6 \mathrm{ m}$. Then, $\angle A D C=75^{{}^{\circ}}$.
$\begin{aligned} & \text{$ From $} \triangle A C D, \angle C A D+\angle A D C+\angle A C D=180^{{}^{\circ}} \\ & \therefore \angle C A D+75^{{}^{\circ}}+90^{{}^{\circ}}=180^{{}^{\circ}} \\ & \therefore \angle C A D=180^{{}^{\circ}}-90^{{}^{\circ}}-75^{{}^{\circ}}=15^{{}^{\circ}}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \text{ As, } A B=B D \text{. } \\ & \therefore \angle C A D=\angle B D A=15^{{}^{\circ}} \text{ and } \\ & \angle B D C=75^{{}^{\circ}}-15^{{}^{\circ}}=60^{{}^{\circ}} \text{. }\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \text{ From } \triangle B C D, \sin \left(60^{{}^{\circ}}\right)=\frac{B C}{B D}=\frac{B C}{6} \\ & \therefore B C=6 \cdot \sin \left(60^{{}^{\circ}}\right)=6 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=3 \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}$ Hence, height of flagstaff $=(6+3 \sqrt{3}) \mathrm{m}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A plane is observed to be approaching the airport. It is at a distance of $10$ km from the point of observation and makes an angle of elevation of $67\cdot5^{}^{\circ}$. What is the height of the plane above the ground ?
questions.solution:
Let $h$ be the height of the plane above the ground.

The distance from the point of observation to the plane is $d = 10$ km.

The angle of elevation is $\theta = 67.5^{}^{\circ}$.

From the right-angled triangle formed, $\sin \theta = \dfrac{h}{d}$.

$h = 10 \sin 67.5^{}^{\circ}$

Using the half-angle formula, $\sin \theta = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \cos 2\theta}{2}}$.

$\sin 67.5^{}^{\circ} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \cos 135^{}^{\circ}}{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \left(-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\sqrt{2} + 1}{2\sqrt{2}}}$

Multiplying the numerator and denominator inside the square root by $\sqrt{2}:

\sin 67.5^{}^{\circ} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 + \sqrt{2}}{4}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2}}}{2}$

Substituting this value into the equation for $h$:

$h = 10 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2}}}{2} = 5\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2}}$ km

Paragraph: A flagstaff 20 m long standing on a pillar 10 m high subtends an angle $\tan ^{-1}(0.5)$ at a point $P$ on the ground. Let $\theta$ be the angle subtended by the pillar at this point $P$.
Question: What is a possible value of $\tan \theta$ ?
questions.solution: $\tan \theta=\frac{10}{x} \Rightarrow \tan \theta=\frac{10}{10}$ or $\frac{10}{30}\tan \theta=1$ or $\frac{1}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The shadow of a tower is found to be $x$ metre longer, when the angle of elevation of the sun changes from $60^{{}^{\circ}}$ to $45^{{}^{\circ}}$. If the height of the tower is $5(3+\sqrt{3}) \mathrm{m}$, then what is $x$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Shadow length when elevation of Sun is $60^{{}^{\circ}}=B C$
From $\triangle A B C$, $B C=A B \cdot \cot \left(60^{{}^{\circ}}\right)=5(3+\sqrt{3}) \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=5(\sqrt{3}+1) \mathrm{m}$ Shadow length when elevation of Sun is $45^{{}^{\circ}}=B D$ From $\triangle A B D$, $B D=A B \cdot \cot 45^{{}^{\circ}}=5(3+\sqrt{3}) \cdot 1=5(3+\sqrt{3}) \mathrm{m}\therefore x=B D-B C=5(3+\sqrt{3})-5(\sqrt{3}+1)=10 \mathrm{ m}$

questions.solution: from figure (iii), $\mathrm{h}^2 \cot ^2 y=\mathrm{z}^2+\mathrm{h}^2 \cot ^2 \mathrm{x}\Rightarrow \mathrm{z}^2=\mathrm{h}^2 \left(\cot ^2 \mathrm{y}-\cot ^2 \mathrm{x}\right)$

questions.q: A balloon is directly above one end of a bridge. The angle of depression of the other end of the bridge from the balloon is $48^{{}^{\circ}}$. If the height of the balloon above the bridge is 122 m , then what is the length of the bridge?
questions.solution:
Let the bridge is BC and height above the bridge $\mathrm{AB}=122 \mathrm{ m}$.
From $\triangle \mathrm{ABC}, \begin{aligned} & \cot 48^{{}^{\circ}}=\frac{\mathrm{BC}}{\mathrm{AB}}=\frac{\mathrm{BC}}{122} \\ & \mathrm{BC}=122 \cdot \cot \left(48^{{}^{\circ}}\right) \\ &= 122 \cdot \cot \left(90^{{}^{\circ}}-42^{{}^{\circ}}\right) \\ &= 122 \cdot \tan 42^{{}^{\circ}} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The top of a hill observed from the top and bottom of a building of height h is at angles of elevation $\frac{\pi}{6}$ and $\frac{\pi}{3}$ respectively. What is the height of the hill?
questions.solution: From question, In $\triangle \mathrm{PQR}$ and $\triangle \mathrm{PST}$. $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{B}=\frac{\mathrm{H}}{\tan \frac{\pi}{3}}=\frac{\mathrm{H}-h}{\tan \frac{\pi}{6}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad & \frac{\mathrm{H}}{3}=\mathrm{H}-h \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{2}{3} \mathrm{H}=h \\ \Rightarrow & \mathrm{H}=\frac{3}{2} h \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
The angles of elevation of the top of a tower from the top and foot of a pole are respectively $30^{{}^{\circ}}$ and $45^{{}^{\circ}}$. If $\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the height of the tower and $h_p$ is the height of the pole, then which of the following are correct?
1. $\frac{2 \mathrm{ h}_{\mathrm{P}} \mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{T}}}{3+\sqrt{3}}=\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{P}^2
2. \frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{T}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{P}}}{\sqrt{3}+1}=\frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{P}}}{2}
3. \frac{2\left(\mathrm{ h}_{\mathrm{P}}+\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{T}}\right)}{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{P}}}=4+\sqrt{3}$
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution:
Let the distance between tower and pole be ' $x$ '.
$\begin{aligned} & \tan 45^{{}^{\circ}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}}{\mathrm{x}} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}}{\mathrm{x}}=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{ h}_{\mathrm{t}}=\mathrm{x} .\end{aligned}$ Now, $\tan 30^{{}^{\circ}}=\frac{h_{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{x}} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{x}}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}-1}=\frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}-\left(\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}\right)}\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2}=\frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\sqrt{3}+1}=\frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{2}$\ldots(1) So, statement ' 2 ' is correct. Now, $\frac{h_t-h_p}{h_p}=\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2} \Rightarrow \frac{h_t-h_p+2 h_p}{h_p}=\frac{\sqrt{3}+1+4}{2}\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}+\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}=\frac{5+\sqrt{3}}{2}$\ldots(2) So, statement ‘3’ is incorrect.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If a flag-staff of 6 m height placed on the top of a tower throws a shadow of $2 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{ m}$ along the ground, then what is the angle that the sun makes with the ground?
questions.solution:
A B$ is the tower. $B Cis flag staff. The angles made by the shadows of $tower and flag staff are same.
\begin{aligned}
& \text{ In } \triangle A B E, \tan \theta=\frac{h}{x}...(1) \\
& \text{ In } \triangle A C D, \tan \theta=\frac{h+6}{x+2 \sqrt{3}}...(2)\\
& \text{ from (1), (2), } \frac{h}{x}=\frac{h+6}{x+2 \sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow h x+2 \sqrt{3} h=h x+6 x \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{h}{x}=\frac{6}{2 \sqrt{3}}=\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{3} \cdot \sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}}=\sqrt{3}
\end{aligned}$
from(1), $\tan \theta=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{x}}=\sqrt{3} \Rightarrow \theta=60^{{}^{\circ}}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A spherical balloon of radius $r$ subtends an angle $\alpha$ at the eye of an observer, while the angle of elevation of its centre is $\beta$. What is the height of the centre of the balloon (neglecting the height of the observer)?
questions.solution:
Let ' $A$ ' be the position of eye. Let ' $O$ ' be the centre of spherical balloon. Let ' $h$ ' be the height of centre of balloon.
From figure, in $\triangle \mathrm{OAD}, \sin \frac{\alpha}{2}=\frac{\mathrm{OD}}{\mathrm{OA}}=\frac{\mathrm{r}}{\mathrm{OA}}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \mathrm{OA}=\frac{\mathrm{r}}{\sin \frac{\alpha}{2}}...(1) \\ & \text{ In } \triangle \mathrm{OAB}, \sin \beta=\frac{\mathrm{OB}}{\mathrm{OA}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{OA}} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{ h}=\mathrm{OA} \cdot \sin \beta \\ & =\frac{\mathrm{r} \cdot \sin \beta}{\sin \frac{\alpha}{2}}...from (1) \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From the top of a lighthouse, 100 m high, the angle of depression of a boat is $\tan ^{-1} \left(\frac{5}{12}\right).$What is the distance between the boat and the lighthouse?
questions.solution:
Given, angle of depression, $\theta=\tan ^{-1} \left(\frac{5}{12}\right)
\begin{aligned}$& \Rightarrow \tan $\theta=\frac{5}{12}\\ \text{$ and $} \Rightarrow \frac{100}{x}=\frac{5}{12}\\ \text{ and } \Rightarrow x=\frac{100 \times 12}{5}=240 \mathrm{ m}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A moving boat is observed from the top of a cliff of 150 m height. The angle of depression of the boat changes from $60^{{}^{\circ}}$ to $45^{{}^{\circ}}$ in 2 minutes. What is the speed of the boat in metres per hour?
questions.solution:
$
\begin{aligned} & \tan 60^{{}^{\circ}}=\frac{150}{x} \Rightarrow x=\frac{150}{\sqrt{3}} \\ & \text{Also, } \tan 45^{{}^{\circ}}=\frac{150}{x+y} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad x+y=150 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad y=150-x=150-\frac{150}{\sqrt{3}} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad y=150\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)=\text{ distance travelled } \\ & \quad \text{ Speed }(\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{hr})=\frac{150(\sqrt{3}-1)}{\sqrt{3}} \times \frac{60}{2}=4500 \frac{(\sqrt{3}-1)}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A lamp post stands on a horizontal plane. From a point situated at a distance 150 m from its foot, the angle of elevation of the top is $30^{{}^{\circ}}$. What is the height of the lamp post?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \tan 30^{{}^{\circ}} & =\frac{h}{150} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & =\frac{h}{150}\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad h=\frac{150}{\sqrt{3}} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}}=50 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{ m}\therefore$ Height of the lamp post $=50 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{ m}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The angles of elevation of the top of a tower standing on a horizontal plane from two points on a line passing through the foot of the tower at distances 49 m and 36 m are $43^{{}^{\circ}}$ and $47^{{}^{\circ}}$ respectively. What is the height of the tower?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{AB}=\mathrm{h} \text{ (height$ of $the tower) } \\ & \mathrm{BD}=36 \mathrm{ m} \\ & \mathrm{BC}=49 \mathrm{ m} \\ & \angle \mathrm{D}=47^{{}^{\circ}} \\ & \angle \mathrm{C}=43^{{}^{\circ}}\end{aligned}$
Now, in $\triangle A B D$, $\tan 47^{{}^{\circ}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{36 \mathrm{ m}}...(i)$ and in $\triangle \mathrm{ABC}$, $\begin{aligned} & \tan 43^{{}^{\circ}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{49 \mathrm{ m}} \\ & \tan \left(90^{{}^{\circ}}-47^{{}^{\circ}}\right)=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{49} \end{aligned}\therefore \quad \cot 47^{{}^{\circ}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{49}...(ii)$ Multiplying equations (i) and (ii) $\begin{aligned} & \tan 47^{{}^{\circ}} \cdot \cot 47^{{}^{\circ}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{36} \times \frac{\mathrm{h}}{49}=1=\frac{\mathrm{h}^2}{36 \times 49} \\ & \mathrm{ h}=6 \times 7=42 \mathrm{ m} \end{aligned}\therefore \quad$ Option (B) is correct

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From an aeroplane above a straight road the angles of depression of two positions at a distance 20 m apart on the road are observed to be $30^{{}^{\circ}}$ and $45^{{}^{\circ}}$. The height of the aeroplane above the ground is:
questions.solution: $\begin{array}{ll}\text{ In } \triangle \mathrm{ABD}, & \tan 45^{{}^{\circ}}=\frac{h}{x} \\ \Rightarrow & 1=\frac{h}{x} \Rightarrow h=x\end{array} In $\triangle $\mathrm{ABC}, \begin{array}{rlrl}$& & \tan 30^{{}^{\circ}} & =$\frac{h}{x+20}$\\ & \Rightarrow \quad $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$& =$\frac{h}{x+20}=\frac{h}{h+20} \quad(\because$x=h) \\ \Rightarrow & \quad $\sqrt{3}$h & =h+20=($\sqrt{3}$h-h)=20 \\ \Rightarrow & h($\sqrt{3}-$1) & =20 \\ \Rightarrow \quad & h & =$\frac{20}{\sqrt{3}-1} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{3}+1}=\frac{20(\sqrt{3}+1)}{2}$\\ \Rightarrow \quad & h & =10($\sqrt{3}+$1) \end{array} Hence, height of the aeroplane above the ground $=10(\sqrt{3}+1) \mathrm{m}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
The top (M$) of a tower is observed from three points $P$, $Q$ and $R$ lying in a horizontal straight line which passes directly along the foot (N$) of the tower. The angles of elevations of $M$ from $P$, $Q$ and $R$ are $30°$, $45°$ and $60°$ respectively. Let $PQ = a$ and $QR = b$.

What is $MN$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Let $MN = h$ be the height of the tower.

The distances of points $P$, $Q$, and $R$ from the foot of the tower $N$ are given by:

$PN = h \cot 30^{{}^{\circ}} = h\sqrt{3}$

$QN = h \cot 45^{{}^{\circ}} = h$

$RN = h \cot 60^{{}^{\circ}} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{3}}$

Given that $P$, $Q$, $R$ lie on a straight line passing through $N$, the distance $QR$ is:

$QR = QN - RN$

$b = h - \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{3}}$

$b = h \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}-1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)

$h = $\dfrac{b\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}-1}

Rationalizing$ the denominator:

h = $\dfrac{b\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}+1)}{(\sqrt{3}-1)(\sqrt{3}+1)}

$h = $\dfrac{b(3+\sqrt{3})}{3-1}

$h = $\left(\dfrac{3+\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$b$

Answer: \left(\dfrac{3+\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)b$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The angles of elevation of the top of a tower from two places situated at distances 21 m and $x \mathrm{ m}$ from the base of the tower are $45^{{}^{\circ}}$ and $60^{{}^{\circ}}$ respectively. What is the value of $x$ ?
questions.solution: Let $A B$ is a tower, Given that $\mathrm{AC}=21 \mathrm{ m}$ and $\mathrm{AD}=x \mathrm{ m}$ From $\triangle \mathrm{ABC}, \tan \left(45^{{}^{\circ}}\right)=\frac{\mathrm{AB}}{\mathrm{AC}}1=\frac{\mathrm{AB}}{21}\therefore A B=21 \mathrm{ m}$ Again, from $\triangle \mathrm{ABD}, \begin{aligned} \tan \left(60^{{}^{\circ}}\right) & =\frac{\mathrm{AB}}{\mathrm{AD}} \Rightarrow \sqrt{3}=\frac{21}{x} \\ x & =7 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{ m} \end{aligned}$
